correctness.rationale: For arbitrary unstructured symmetric kernels, compression trace gives \(\mu\ge1-T/m\) and the contrast Rayleigh quotient gives \(\mu\ge\lvert1-T(1/k+1/m)\rvert\). Their sharp scalar minimax fixes total cross mass. Saturation of positive-semidefinite upper/lower bounds gives eigenvector equalities forcing uniform cross-edge weights in each optimizer. Orthogonal decomposition into constant, leaf-zero-sum, contrast and core-zero-sum spaces gives exact necessary-and-sufficient core Laplacian spectral interval; canonical complete-core and zero-core witnesses prove sharp transition regimes. Boundaries \(m=k\) and \(m=2k\) included. Standalone exact rational checks and LP tests passed 3343 assertions; finite tests are not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2007/2009 complete-multipartite SDP and 2025 clique-lift theorem closely cover the same graph and the latter covers the optimal SLEM plus one canonical optimum. They do not state a classification of every unrestricted asymmetric optimum, the spectral core-face conditions, necessity of connected core support at \(m<k\), optional core edges at \(k\le m<2k\), or unique optimum at \(m\ge2k\). The full optimizer face and equality-based rigidity, not the optimal value, are the assessed contribution. Other, unindexed formulations remain a substantive risk.
residual_risks: Jafarizadeh’s broad clique-lift theorem may have consequences for all optimizers not explicitly presented as such; the originality claim is limited to direct full-face classification and edge-support phase transitions.
A specialized paper on SDP optimal faces, equi-optimal network weights, or split graphs could contain equivalent equality conditions under different terminology.
Semantic indexing is incomplete; absence of a retrieved result is not novelty proof.

value.rationale: Exact family-wide optimizer-face classification for the natural symmetric stochastic mixing problem, with two sharp parameter thresholds that decide whether internal core communication is obligatory, optional or impossible at the optimal mixing rate. It yields a connectedness constraint and uniqueness boundary for unrestricted edge allocations and can guide secondary cost or robustness selection without degrading asymptotic convergence. This information is not implied by reporting one optimal transition matrix.
